clue.text: Became excited when the class went first

parts.note: a kind is a class or sort of thing
to lead is to go first, past tense led

explanation.surface: Pupils grew animated once their form was allowed to go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings that are kindled have been set alight, so the person has become aroused or stirred up.

clue.text: Spoilsport will murder the girl

parts.note: to murder is to kill
Joy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A threat that someone will do away with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket who stops others having fun is a spoilsport.

clue.text: Not clever to be striking

parts.note: an able person is clever or capable

explanation.surface: Being dim is not the way to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable or worthy of notice is striking.

clue.text: Swirling oil about on French river

indicators.note: something swirling is churned round, so the letters of the next word are stirred into a new order

parts.note: re is a short Latin-derived word for about or concerning

explanation.surface: Oil slicks eddying on a waterway in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing west to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Gifts from the same countries

parts.note: do is short for ditto, meaning the same again
nations are countries

explanation.surface: Presents sent from a group of states with identical aims.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, the abbreviation of ditto, is the old list-writer's mark for 'the same as above'.
explanation.definitionFit: Donations are contributions given freely, that is, gifts.

clue.text: Knightly companion friend, a big noise

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: A noble knight's mate who makes a terrible racket.
explanation.definitionFit: The paladins were the twelve peers attending Charlemagne, so a knight in his company.

clue.text: Minister ofthe armed forces

parts.note: reads like a government defence secretary, but means a clergyman serving soldiers, sailors or airmen

explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the familiar title of a military chaplain, a minister of religion attached to the services.

clue.text: It is profitable to have most of the good fortune with four in charge

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: luck is good fortune

indicators.note: in places the Roman numeral inside the word for a charge

parts.note: a rate is a charge or price
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Being in luck with a small foursome in control pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims LUCK to LUC; 'in' puts IV inside RATE to give RATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinning venture is profitable, bringing in plenty of gain.

clue.text: Flighty creature on the way up is allowed a small quantity

indicators.note: in a down clue a word heading upwards is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a bird is a creature that flies
something allowed is let

explanation.surface: A bird climbing skyward is permitted a tiny portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns BIRD into DRIB.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a little drop or trickle, hence a tiny amount.

clue.text: Failure to exercise a right when one runs round

indicators.note: the letters are spun round into a different order

explanation.surface: A legal entitlement lapses when a person goes running in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, nonuser is the neglect of a privilege, which may cause it to be lost.

clue.text: Disinclined to have a Scotsman in the Edinburgh area

parts.note: loth means reluctant or disinclined
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Reluctance to welcome a Scot into the capital's surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: LOTHIAN is the region of Scotland that contains Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lothians form the historic region around Scotland's capital city.

clue.text: Manner of speaking sends CID into confusion

indicators.note: being put into confusion means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Detectives are thrown by the way someone talks.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives; here it is just letters for the anagram with INTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Diction is enunciation, the style in which words are pronounced.

clue.text: Is it at the heart of employment activity?

definitions.text: Is it at the heart of employment activity?

parts.words: Is it at the heart of employment activity?
parts.note: the centre of work-finding is literally an office for job seekers

explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is a British government office where the unemployed look for work.
explanation.definitionFit: A British public office helping people find work is literally a hub for jobs.

clue.text: Drinks about ten pins

indicators.note: the drinks go round, enclosing the numeral

parts.note: ales are drinks
X is ten in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Beers all round for the ten-pin bowlers.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is a spindle or pin on which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Give way to the crop

definitions.meaning: the amount produced by a harvest

explanation.surface: Surrendering to the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To give in is to submit; and a harvest's output is its produce.

clue.text: It is unsafe, Daniel, with grouse all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Danny is in peril, with game birds flying everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' scrambles GROUSE into GEROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous or risky is unsafe.

clue.text: Haberdasher should come from hospital thus

parts.note: a discharged patient is out
in that state, that is, healthier

explanation.surface: A draper ought to be discharged from the ward in better shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a patient who should come OUT of hospital FITTER than before.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfitter sells clothing and accessories, a role close to a haberdasher's.

clue.text: However this is not a trial game

definitions.text: However this is not a trial game

parts.words: However this is not a trial game
parts.note: the name of an international cricket fixture sounds like a trial run, yet it is the real contest

explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket match, the highest form of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Despite the word test in its name, an international cricket fixture is the full contest, not a trial.

clue.text: Spotting of measles perhaps

parts.note: spotting suggests the rash of spots, but means identifying the illness

explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's identification of a disease from its symptoms is the medical conclusion.

clue.text: Harmed old mother first

indicators.note: the word for mother comes before the word for old

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
aged means old

explanation.surface: An elderly mum got hurt before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Something damaged has been hurt or impaired.

clue.text: Placate a parish priest with ease

explanation.surface: Soothe a vicar comfortably.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify or calm someone is to placate them.

clue.text: A number had a meal, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: ate is had a meal

explanation.surface: Several people dined, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure after seven is a number.

clue.text: Merry despite breaking leg on damaged flue

indicators.note: a broken word has its letters rearranged
a damaged word is knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Cheerful though they fractured a limb on a broken chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' turns LEG into GLE and 'damaged' turns FLUE into EFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Merry and joyful mean the same thing.

clue.text: Model did some fishing and got the lines in a confused mess

definitions.text: got the lines in a confused mess

parts.note: the Model T was the famous Ford car
angled means fished with rod and line

explanation.surface: A fashion model went fishing and knotted her lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines twisted into knots have been snarled up.

clue.text: Chart the continental tree

parts.note: a map is a chart
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Plotting a tree found on the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple, source of syrup, is a tree.

clue.text: Arrive washed so admit

parts.note: to come is to arrive
washed things are clean

explanation.surface: Turn up freshly bathed and confess.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess the truth fully is to own up.

clue.text: Better preserved

definitions.meaning: kept from spoiling by salting or smoking

explanation.surface: Improved and kept from going off.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient who has recovered is healed; meat salted or smoked has been kept.

clue.text: Round number in a tin

indicators.note: one word goes inside the container

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A whole figure stored inside a metal container.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a musical piece in which voices enter in turn, like a round.

clue.text: Bewitching charm of heartless girl having a love-affair

parts.note: amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted young woman with a lover has magnetic allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes IR from GIRL, leaving GL.
explanation.definitionFit: Glamour originally meant a magic spell, hence enchanting allure.

clue.text: Musical version from a French flute

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a rearrangement

parts.note: un is French for a

explanation.surface: A rendition played on a French flute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something melodious or tuneful is musical.

clue.text: Being fully clothed, prepared for cooking

definitions.meaning: of poultry or game, cleaned and readied for the pot

explanation.surface: Dressed up, or ready for the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has put on garments; poultry cleaned and trussed ready for the oven.

clue.text: Seaman showed the way but committed afoul

parts.note: a hand is a crew member on a ship
led means guided

explanation.surface: A sailor took the lead but broke the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, handling the ball is a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer touching the ball with the arm has committed handball, an infringement.
